audit.main_at_report_time: e745a0a (PRs #6/#7: buyer-web styling, Vercel Analytics, scripts/create-test-seller.mjs; no changes under seller-app/, supabase/ or .github/ — findings unaffected)

priority_scale.P1: fix before production launch if practical

findings.title: Reaper runs ~5x/day instead of every 5 min; holds last hours
findings.screen_workflow: Buyer abandons checkout during a live → piece should return to sale after 15 min
findings.description: Expired holds are only released by release_expired_holds(), run from a GitHub Actions schedule. GitHub actually ran it about 5 times a day (median gap 5 h 07 min, max 7 h 42 min over the last 30 scheduled runs) instead of every 5 minutes. Checkout does not treat an expired, unclaimed hold as available, so an abandoned cart removes a unique piece from sale for hours.
findings.reproduction: List scheduled runs of reaper-cron.yml; during a test live, abandon a checkout and watch the piece stay 'Reserved' past 15 minutes.
findings.root_cause: Best-effort CI scheduler used as a production job runner; no lazy expiry in the reservation RPC.
findings.impact: Every abandoned checkout locks a piece for the rest of the live; buyers see 'Reserved' on pieces nobody will pay for; the seller must spot and Force Release them manually (which itself is unsafe, SA-PAY-005).
findings.recommended_remediation: Run the reaper inside Postgres (pg_cron every minute) or a Supabase scheduled Edge Function; add lazy expiry inside create_order_with_reservation (an expired, unclaimed hold is released under the same row lock); alert on reaper lag.
findings.regression_test: SQL test: checkout of a piece with an expired unclaimed hold succeeds; hosted check H9 (expired-but-pending count) returns 0 within 2 minutes.

findings.title: Late advance verified as full payment (order paid, ledger shows advance)
findings.screen_workflow: Payments tab → 'Late Claim' card → Verify Payment
findings.description: When a late claim is verified and the pieces are still available, the RPC marks the order fully paid (status=paid, payment_status=paid, total_paid_paisa=total_paisa, balance_due=0) regardless of payment_type. A late ₹250 advance on a ₹2,500 order becomes 'paid in full'; the ledger row records ₹250.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/13_payments.out: FINDING 13.5c 'order paid/paid total=250000 total_paid=250000 balance_due=0 | ledger records advance=25000'
findings.reproduction: Advance order → advance attempt → hold expires (reaper) → buyer submits UTR (late_claim_pending_review) → seller verifies. Suite 13.5.
findings.root_cause: Late branch hard-codes the full-payment transition instead of reusing the per-type transition.
findings.impact: Seller ships a ₹2,500 garment after receiving ₹250 (the label also prints 'PREPAID - DO NOT COLLECT CASH', SA-SHIP-002); order totals disagree with the ledger; analytics overstate revenue.
findings.recommended_remediation: In the late branch apply the same per-type transition as the on-time path (advance → confirmed/advance_paid with balance due); add an invariant check total_paid_paisa = SUM(verified order_payments.amount_paisa).
findings.regression_test: Suite 13.5 must end with payment_status=advance_paid and balance_due = total − advance; ledger sum = total_paid.

findings.title: Late-claim verification race sells one piece to two buyers
findings.screen_workflow: Seller verifies a late claim while buyers keep checking out during the live
findings.description: The late branch reads availability with bool_and(p.status='available') without a lock, then locks and sets status='sold' with no status predicate. A checkout that reserves the same piece in between is overwritten: the late-claim order becomes paid, the new order keeps a pending reservation on a piece now marked sold with reserved_by_order_id=NULL; when that buyer pays and is verified, two fully paid orders contain one unique garment.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/14_concurrency.out: FINDING 14.2 (X=paid/paid, Y=pending/unpaid, piece=sold reserved_by=NULL) and FINDING 14.2b (paid orders containing the single piece #A02 = 2)
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/sql/14_concurrency.sh scenario 14.2 (session B holds an uncommitted checkout for 3 s while the seller verifies).
findings.root_cause: Check-then-act outside the row lock; UPDATE lacks AND status='available'; no constraint preventing one product from belonging to two live orders.
findings.impact: Double sale of a one-of-a-kind piece — refund, apology, reputational damage — most likely exactly when a seller clears late claims during a busy live.
findings.recommended_remediation: Lock products FOR UPDATE (ORDER BY id) before evaluating availability; UPDATE ... WHERE status='available' and check row count; route to the refund-required path otherwise; add a partial unique index or sold_to_order_id constraint so a product can belong to only one non-cancelled order.
findings.regression_test: 14_concurrency.sh 14.2 must end with exactly one paid order for #A02 and the late claim flagged refund-required.

findings.title: Buyer-claimed payments silently expire after 24 h and vanish
findings.screen_workflow: Buyer has paid and submitted a UTR; seller does not act within 24 h
findings.description: A buyer claim extends the hold to 24 h. If the seller has not verified by then, the reaper sets the attempt to 'expired', cancels the order and releases the piece. 'expired' is not in the seller queue filter and cancelled orders are hidden from the Kanban, so a real payment silently disappears from the app.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/13_payments.out: FINDING 13.8 'order=cancelled attempt=expired piece=available still in seller queue=0'
audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T20 (cancelled/expired orders not shown in any Kanban tab)
findings.reproduction: Suite 13.8: claim → move clock/verification window past 24 h → reaper → query the queue.
findings.root_cause: The reaper treats a buyer-claimed (money-in-flight) attempt like an unpaid hold.
findings.impact: Buyer money received with no order and no visible record; disputes and chargebacks; most likely during festival peaks when sellers fall behind.
findings.recommended_remediation: Never auto-expire an attempt with a buyer UTR: move it to late_claim_pending_review (or a 'needs_review' state) and keep it in the queue; alert the seller before the window ends (needs SA-NOT-001); show time remaining on each claim.
findings.regression_test: Suite 13.8 must leave the attempt reviewable and returned by getPendingVerifications().

findings.title: Refund-owed late payments are invisible in the app
findings.component: verify late claim with pieces gone (supabase/migrations/023_late_upi_recovery.sql:438-505) + seller-app/lib/presentation/pending_verifications_screen.dart:112-121 + Kanban filters
findings.screen_workflow: Payments tab → Late Claim → Verify (garment already resold)
findings.description: Verifying a late claim for pieces that were resold records a verified payment, sets payment_status='paid' on a cancelled order, appends a note and returns refund_required=true. The app ignores the response (snackbar 'Payment verified for Order #…'), cancelled orders appear in no Kanban tab, and there is no refund status, queue or reminder anywhere.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/13_payments.out: FINDING 13.6 'rpc success=true refund_required=true | order status=cancelled payment=paid notes=LATE_CLAIM_PAYMENT_VERIFIED…'
findings.reproduction: Suite 13.6; then open the seller app — the order is not listed anywhere.
findings.root_cause: Refund obligation modelled only as free text in orders.notes and a transient RPC field.
findings.impact: The seller owes the buyer money and nothing in the product tracks it — consumer complaints, UPI disputes, legal exposure.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add refund_status/refund_amount_paisa (or a refunds table) set atomically by the RPC; show a red 'Refund owed' item in an Exception Center; the verify dialog must warn 'garment already sold — you must refund ₹X' before confirming; record refund reference when done.
findings.regression_test: Suite 13.6 asserts refund_status='required'; widget test: verify response with refund_required → refund dialog + order listed under Exceptions.

findings.title: Anonymous users can rewrite/delete seller storefront rows via public_seller_storefronts
findings.screen_workflow: Buyer storefront / every approved seller's profile; reachable with the public anon key, no login
findings.description: The public storefront projection is a simple single-table view over profiles. Supabase's default privileges grant ALL on new public objects to anon/authenticated; the migrations only add GRANT SELECT and never revoke INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE. The view is not security_invoker, so DML through it runs with the owner's rights and bypasses the profiles RLS policies. Anyone holding the anon key (it ships in the buyer-web bundle) can rewrite or delete approved sellers' storefront rows.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/10_exposure_and_view_dml.out: FINDING 10.3 anon UPDATE rows=1 (store_name, phone_number=9000000000, upi_enabled=f, default_shipping_fee_paisa=999900, advance_amount_paisa=100)
audit/seller-app/evidence/10_exposure_and_view_dml.out: FINDING 10.4 anon DELETE of an approved seller with no drops (rows=1); FINDING 10.5 seller B rewrote seller A's store_slug

audit/seller-app/evidence/10_exposure_and_view_dml.out: INFO 10.9 anon holds DELETE, INSERT, UPDATE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER on the view; control PASS 10.6 (base-table UPDATE of another seller = 0 rows)
supabase/migrations/033_hide_seller_upi_from_public_storefronts.sql:9-30 (DROP/CREATE VIEW, GRANT SELECT only; no REVOKE, no security_invoker)
audit/seller-app/tests/sql/00_supabase_shim.sql reproduces Supabase's documented default ACLs; hosted confirmation: audit/seller-app/tests/sql/90_hosted_readonly_checks.sql H1-H2 + curl probe
findings.reproduction: Local: tests/sql/run_local_db_audit.sh (suite 10). Hosted, non-destructive: curl -X PATCH "$SUPABASE_URL/rest/v1/public_seller_storefronts?id=eq.00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" -H "apikey: $ANON" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANON" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"store_name":"x"}' — a secure project answers 401/403 (42501); a vulnerable one answers 200/204 with an empty result. Never target a real seller id.
findings.root_cause: Default privileges + auto-updatable view without security_invoker and without an explicit REVOKE of write privileges.
findings.impact: During a live, an anonymous attacker can: swap the boutique phone number so buyers' 'Chat with boutique'/WhatsApp goes to the attacker (payment-redirection fraud); set upi_enabled=false so reservations continue but no buyer can pay (see SA-PAY-012); poison shipping fee/free-shipping threshold/advance amount used by checkout; hijack store_slug links; delete newly approved sellers' profiles (sellers with drops are protected only by FK RESTRICT).
findings.recommended_remediation: New migration: REVOKE ALL ON public.public_seller_storefronts FROM anon, authenticated; GRANT SELECT ON ... TO anon, authenticated; recreate the view WITH (security_invoker = true) (or expose a SECURITY DEFINER read function); repeat for every public view; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON TABLES FROM anon, authenticated; add a CI catalog test that fails if anon/authenticated hold any DML privilege on a view.
findings.regression_test: tests/sql/10_exposure_and_view_dml.sql 10.3-10.5 must report 0 rows / permission denied and 10.9 must list SELECT only; hosted H1/H2 must return no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE grants for anon/authenticated.
findings.confidence: High (local, Supabase default ACLs reproduced). Hosted state not yet probed: run H1/H2.

findings.title: Seller password in public Git history; rotation unverified
findings.component: Git history: scripts/seed-legitimate-staging-drop.mjs (commit 0abdaeb, removed from HEAD in ebb80cd)
findings.screen_workflow: Seller login for the account used by the staging seed script; repository hygiene
findings.description: A seller e-mail and password for the Supabase project referenced by the seed script were committed on 2026-09-26 and only removed from HEAD on 2026-10-03. The repository is public, so the credential remains retrievable from history and from any clone/fork made in between. Whether the password was rotated and sessions revoked cannot be verified from the repository; this audit deliberately did not try the credential.
evidence: git show 0abdaeb:scripts/seed-legitimate-staging-drop.mjs lines 10-14 (SUPABASE_URL, SELLER_EMAIL, SELLER_PASSWORD — value redacted here)
git show ebb80cd -- scripts/seed-legitimate-staging-drop.mjs (replaced with STAGING_SELLER_EMAIL/STAGING_SELLER_PASSWORD env vars)
docs/audit/08-CONFIG-AUDIT.md:7 and docs/audit/FINAL-PRODUCTION-READINESS-REPORT.md:27 (AUD-001: rotate + purge history) — no rotation record exists in the repo
findings.reproduction: git log -p -S SELLER_PASSWORD -- scripts/seed-legitimate-staging-drop.mjs on any clone. Do not use the credential.
findings.root_cause: Credentials hard-coded in a tracked script; no secret scanning or push protection.
findings.impact: If still valid: full seller takeover — buyer PII (names, phones, addresses), payment verification/rejection, hold release, and changing the payee UPI VPA so buyers pay an attacker. If this project is the one real buyers use, it is a platform trust incident.
findings.recommended_remediation: Rotate the password and revoke all sessions for that user now (Supabase dashboard → Authentication → Users); review Auth logs since 2026-09-26; purge the blob from history (git filter-repo) and force-push in a coordinated window; enable GitHub secret scanning + push protection and a gitleaks CI job; use ephemeral per-run test accounts.
findings.regression_test: CI secret-scan job (gitleaks) on every push; written rotation record in docs/ops.
findings.confidence: High for exposure; validity unknown (not tested by design).

findings.title: Release signed with debug key; CI ships a debug APK
findings.screen_workflow: Distribution of the APK to real sellers
findings.description: The release build type is signed with the debug key and CI only produces a debug APK artifact (debuggable, built with the staging URL/anon key). The first APK handed to sellers fixes the signing identity: later builds signed differently cannot be installed as updates without uninstalling (which deletes the intake queue and session).
findings.reproduction: Inspect the signing certificate of the CI artifact (apksigner verify --print-certs).
findings.root_cause: Template default never replaced.
findings.impact: Unupgradeable installs and possible data loss; Play Store rejection; debuggable builds in sellers' hands.
findings.recommended_remediation: Create an upload/release keystore (stored as CI secrets), sign release builds in CI, version codes, distribute via Play internal testing.
findings.regression_test: CI step verifying the release certificate fingerprint.

findings.title: Invalid product codes/titles accepted, shown as Available, fail silently
findings.screen_workflow: Rapid intake → edit the suggested code (e.g. 'A5', '101', 'SAREE01', 'A-07')
findings.description: The code field accepts any text (and the title field any length, while the CHECK allows ≤100 characters); the only validation is the database CHECK. The item is queued, the seller sees 'Piece saved! Syncing to cloud…', the inventory lists it as 'Available', and the insert later fails with 23514 in the background. The queue retries forever and the banner says 'Storage or network error. Tap to retry.' The garment never reaches buyers.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/12_lifecycle_guards.out: INFO 12.1 codes A05, #SAREE01, #A-07 and # rejected with 23514
audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T17 'lastError=… 23514 products_code_check' (surfaces only in the background)
products_inventory_screen.dart:86 (queued items rendered with status available); 249-253 (generic banner text)
findings.reproduction: In intake, change the code to '101', save, open Products: the piece shows Available; the buyer catalog never shows it.
findings.root_cause: No client-side validation/normalisation matching the DB rule; queue does not classify permanent errors; optimistic UI shows queued items as live.
findings.impact: Garments announced on the live cannot be bought; the seller cannot tell why; retries waste battery/data.
findings.recommended_remediation: Normalise and validate the code at entry (auto-prefix '#', uppercase, max 6, A-Z/0-9) with inline error; show queued items as 'Syncing'/'Failed: invalid code — edit'; classify 23514/23505 as permanent with an edit action.
findings.regression_test: Widget test: '101' becomes '#101' or is blocked; queue test: 23514 → status needs_edit (no retry loop).

findings.title: 'Release' cancels orders whose buyer already paid and claimed
findings.screen_workflow: Orders → Pending → Release (buyer has already paid and submitted a UTR)
findings.description: force_release_hold cancels any pending order and returns its pieces to sale without looking at payment attempts. The Release button is shown on every pending card and its dialog does not mention a claim. If the buyer already claimed, the attempt stays 'awaiting_seller_verification' on a cancelled order: it still appears in the Payments queue, but Verify fails with INVALID_ORDER_STATE, and the piece can be bought by someone else. close_drop (024) handles the same situation correctly.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/16_release_and_close_with_claims.out: FINDING 16.1b 'release=true | order=cancelled piece=available attempt=awaiting_seller_verification still in seller queue=1 | verify afterwards -> INVALID_ORDER_STATE'
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/sql/16_release_and_close_with_claims.sql (16.1).
findings.root_cause: 009-era RPC predates the payment-attempt model (013/023); UI has no claim awareness on the order card.
findings.impact: One tap turns a paid order into an unrecordable payment plus an untracked refund obligation; the piece may be resold to another buyer.
findings.recommended_remediation: In force_release_hold refuse (or require an explicit override) when an attempt is buyer_claimed/awaiting_seller_verification/late_claim_pending_review; show 'Payment claim pending — verify or reject first' on the card; hide Release while a claim exists.
findings.regression_test: Suite 16.1 must return an error such as PAYMENT_CLAIM_PENDING and leave order/piece/attempt unchanged.

findings.title: No live updates on Home/Products/Payments; Kanban only per selected drop
findings.screen_workflow: During a live: new reservations, payment claims, pieces becoming reserved/sold
findings.description: Only the Orders tab subscribes to Realtime, and only when a single drop is selected — the default 'All Drops' view has no subscription. Dashboard counters, Products (available/reserved/sold) and the Payments queue never update by themselves; the seller must pull to refresh each tab. The publication does include products, orders and payment_attempts.
evidence: no Realtime usage outside data/realtime/seller_order_realtime.dart and the Kanban
docs/06-requirements-traceability-matrix.md claims realtime dashboard/kanban 'Implemented'; docs/22 budget: order push < 2 s
findings.reproduction: Open the app on Home; place an order from the buyer site → nothing changes until manual refresh.
findings.root_cause: Realtime built as a per-drop Kanban feature, not as an app-wide live state.
findings.impact: The seller works blind during the live: misses claims (leading to SA-PAY-003), announces pieces already reserved, and verifies late.
findings.recommended_remediation: One app-level live session store subscribed to orders, payment_attempts and products for the active drop (seller-scoped), driving Home, Products, Orders and Payments badges; reconnect + catch-up refetch on resume.
findings.regression_test: Widget test with a fake realtime stream: new claim increments the Payments badge and appears in the queue without refresh.

findings.title: Password reset cannot be completed
findings.component: seller-app/lib/presentation/auth/seller_login_screen.dart:124-140; AndroidManifest.xml (no deep-link intent filter); buyer-web (no reset route); supabase/config.toml:158 site_url
findings.screen_workflow: Login → Forgot password?
findings.description: resetPasswordForEmail is called without redirectTo; the e-mailed link goes to the project's Site URL; the app registers no deep link and buyer-web has no password-update page, so the seller cannot set a new password.
findings.reproduction: Request a reset e-mail and open the link on the phone.
findings.root_cause: Recovery flow never completed end-to-end.
findings.impact: A seller who forgets the password is locked out until an operator intervenes in the dashboard — possibly right before a live.
findings.recommended_remediation: Deep link (App Link) handling for type=recovery with an in-app 'Set new password' screen, or a hosted reset page; set redirectTo and allowed redirect URLs.
findings.regression_test: Device test of the full reset flow; widget test of the new-password screen.
findings.confidence: High (code); hosted Site URL not inspected.

findings.title: No push or local notifications; settings toggles are fake
findings.screen_workflow: Seller is streaming in Facebook/Instagram (seller app in background)
findings.description: The app has no push or local notifications of any kind, yet Settings shows 'New orders', 'Payment claims' and 'Hold expiries' toggles that only flip local booleans.
evidence: seller_settings_screen.dart:33-35 local bools; 554-583 switches with no side effects
findings.reproduction: Background the app, place an order and a claim from the buyer site: nothing alerts the seller.
findings.root_cause: Not implemented; UI placeholder.
findings.impact: During a live the seller app is usually in the background or on a second phone; claims wait unseen (feeds SA-PAY-003 and SA-PAY-007); the fake toggles create false assurance.
findings.recommended_remediation: FCM (data messages) triggered by DB events (Edge Function/webhook) for new claim, late claim, new order and claim-expiring; Android 13 notification permission flow; tap opens the right item; remove or wire the toggles.
findings.regression_test: Edge Function test for payload; device checklist (permission denied/granted, tap routing).

findings.title: No crash reporting/telemetry; 33 swallowed errors
findings.component: Whole seller app (33 `catch (_)` blocks; no crash reporting, analytics or remote logging)
findings.screen_workflow: All
findings.description: There is no crash reporting (Crashlytics/Sentry), no structured logging and no client telemetry. 33 catch-all blocks swallow errors, including dashboard data loads, realtime payload parsing, recent activity (returns []), the intake manifest load and registration profile upsert.
evidence: grep 'catch (_)' seller-app/lib → 33 hits (e.g. main.dart:207, seller_dashboard_screen.dart:65-95, seller_order_realtime.dart:57,79, offline_intake_queue.dart:169, seller_registration_screen.dart:147, seller_repository.dart:884)
findings.reproduction: Make any dashboard request fail: the screen shows zeros/empty state with no error and nothing is reported.
findings.root_cause: No observability layer was planned for the client; 'graceful' empty catches.
findings.impact: Production failures are invisible to the seller and the operator; a live can silently degrade (empty dashboards that look like 'no orders').
findings.recommended_remediation: Add crash reporting with release symbols, a small logger that records error codes, and visible error states; replace empty catches with typed handling; server-side: log RPC errors and reaper results.
findings.regression_test: Widget tests: each screen renders an error state when its repository call throws.

findings.title: Intake queue in cache dir; corrupt manifest loses all items
findings.screen_workflow: Rapid intake with poor connectivity; app killed; phone storage pressure
findings.description: The intake queue stores its manifest and photos under Directory.systemTemp (the app cache directory on Android, which the OS or 'Clear cache' may purge); an unreadable manifest is silently ignored and the next save overwrites it, discarding every queued item; the queue is not processed at app start (only initialised) and has no connectivity trigger, so items wait until the camera screen is reopened or the inventory 'Retry' is tapped; an item enqueued while a sync is running is not picked up by that run. ADR-006 (SQLite, connectivity_plus, delete-on-sync, block go-live until synced) is not followed.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T14 (baseDir=/tmp/livedrop_intake_queue = systemTemp), T19 (corrupt manifest drops all items), T18 (second item stays pending)
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_offline_queue_test.dart (T14, T18, T19).
findings.root_cause: JSON-file queue in a cache location; no lifecycle/connectivity integration.
findings.impact: Lost intake work (photos + prices) before a live; items silently not uploaded.
findings.recommended_remediation: Move to the app documents/support directory with atomic writes (write-temp-then-rename) or SQLite as ADR-006 specifies; process on app start/resume and on connectivity regained; re-scan for new items after each run; surface a persistent sync badge.
findings.regression_test: T14/T18/T19 inverted (durable dir, picked up in same run or immediately after, corrupt manifest recovered from backup).

findings.title: Late advance on a resold piece cannot be recorded (constraint error)
findings.component: verify late branch, unavailable pieces + advance (supabase/migrations/023_late_upi_recovery.sql:480-486)
findings.screen_workflow: Payments → Late Claim (advance) → Verify, garment already resold
findings.description: For a late ADVANCE claim whose pieces were resold, the RPC sets total_paid_paisa=advance and balance_due_paisa=0, violating chk_orders_balance_formula. The whole verification fails with a raw constraint error; the seller can neither record the real payment nor mark it for refund (only 'Reject', which tells the buyer the money was not found).
findings.reproduction: Suite 13.7.
findings.root_cause: balance_due hard-coded to 0 instead of total − paid (and order is cancelled, so the formula needs a refund-aware model).
findings.impact: Real money cannot be recorded; the seller is pushed toward a false rejection; raw database text is shown to the seller.
findings.recommended_remediation: Fix together with SA-PAY-001/004: compute balances per type, mark refund_required, never violate the balance invariant; map DB errors to seller-friendly messages.
findings.regression_test: Suite 13.7 must succeed with refund_required and a consistent balance.

findings.title: Any fake UTR locks a piece for 24 hours
findings.screen_workflow: Buyer checkout during a live → 'I have paid' with any text
findings.description: Any 6-35 character alphanumeric string is accepted as a UTR and immediately extends the 15-minute hold to 24 hours. A careless or malicious buyer (or a competitor) can lock the best pieces for a day by typing a fake UTR; only the seller's manual Reject frees them.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/13_payments.out: FINDING 13.2 'fabricated UTR "NOTAREALUTR" moved hold from 00:15:00 to 1 day'
findings.reproduction: Suite 13.2.
findings.root_cause: Claim submission is unauthenticated proof; the extension is unconditional and uncapped during a live drop.
findings.impact: Inventory griefing during the live; combined with SA-RT-001/SA-NOT-001 the seller may not notice for a long time.
findings.recommended_remediation: During a live drop cap the claim-extended hold (e.g. 60-120 min) and escalate to the seller; numeric 12-digit UTR format check for UPI; rate-limit claims per phone/device; show 'claimed, unverified' pieces distinctly with one-tap reject.
findings.regression_test: SQL test: claim during a live drop extends hold by at most the configured cap.

findings.title: Free-shipping threshold computed four ways; drop threshold ignored
findings.component: Shipping-fee rule in four places: create_order_with_reservation (supabase/migrations/022_checkout_idempotency_conflict_detection.sql:212-217, profile threshold only), buyer-web DropHeader.tsx:105-106 (drop threshold), CheckoutReview.tsx:32 (drop ?? profile), CartDrawer.tsx:143 (profile ?? ₹2,000)
findings.screen_workflow: Seller sets 'Free shipping above ₹X' on a drop (create_drop_screen.dart:280) → buyers check out
findings.description: The server ignores the drop's free_shipping_threshold_paisa and uses only the profile threshold; the buyer UI shows three different rules. Totals differ from what the seller configured and from what the buyer was shown. Every profile defaults to a ₹2,000 threshold (001_create_profiles.sql:25) that the seller cannot see or edit in Settings, so clearing the drop threshold does not turn free shipping off.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/13_payments.out: FINDING 13.10a (drop threshold ₹2,999, subtotal ₹2,500 → shipping ₹0) and 13.10b (drop threshold ₹1,000, subtotal ₹1,500 → shipping ₹80 although the banner promised free shipping)
findings.reproduction: Suite 13.10; open the buyer drop page and cart for the same drop.
findings.root_cause: Threshold precedence never specified in one place; RPC not updated when drop-level thresholds were added.
findings.impact: Seller loses shipping fees or buyers are charged more than displayed; the UPI amount differs from what the buyer expected, causing payment mismatches and rejected claims.
findings.recommended_remediation: Define precedence (drop ?? profile ?? none) once in the RPC and return the computed shipping in a quote RPC that all buyer components use; add parity tests across RPC and buyer-web.
findings.regression_test: SQL 13.10a/b + Vitest parity test using the same fixtures.

findings.title: Shipping shortcut ships the first order with a placeholder AWB
findings.screen_workflow: Home → Shipping quick action
findings.description: The shortcut opens the label screen for whatever order is first in the list (any status, usually the newest pending one). The tracking field is pre-filled with the placeholder 'DVA123456789'; the primary button 'Generate & Share Label' actually calls mark_order_shipped immediately, with no confirmation; 'Auto' invents a tracking number from the clock; Share, Print and Download all run the same print call.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T08 'markOrderShipped calls: [{orderId: order-1, tracking: DVA123456789, courier: Delhivery}]' on a pending order
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_home_shell_test.dart (T08). Server-side, unpaid/not-ready orders are rejected (12.8b) — a paid+ready order would be shipped with the fake AWB.
findings.root_cause: Prototype screen wired to the real RPC.
findings.impact: Buyers receive fake tracking numbers; the seller believes labels were shared; confusion on unpaid orders.
findings.recommended_remediation: Remove the shortcut or make it open a 'Ready to ship' list; empty tracking field; separate 'Print label' from 'Mark shipped' with confirmation; real share/download.
findings.regression_test: T08 inverted: shortcut lists only ready orders; no ship call without explicit tracking.

findings.title: No deep links / App Links
findings.screen_workflow: Password recovery links, e-mail confirmation, future notification taps
findings.description: No deep-link or App Link intent filters are declared, so no external link can open a specific screen in the app.
findings.reproduction: adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d https://<domain>/seller/... → no handler.
findings.root_cause: Not designed.
findings.impact: Blocks SA-AUTH-001 and actionable notifications (SA-NOT-001).
findings.recommended_remediation: Verified App Links for a seller domain path + route handling.
findings.regression_test: Device test.

findings.title: No physical-device validation evidence
findings.screen_workflow: All (cold start, camera, printing, share, WhatsApp/UPI intents, background/foreground, low memory)
findings.description: No physical-device evidence exists in the repository and none could be produced here (no Android SDK/emulator; dl.google.com blocked). Performance targets in docs/22 (Redmi 9A-class: cold start < 2.5 s, compression < 600 ms) are unverified.
evidence: Audit environment: Android SDK download blocked; no device
findings.reproduction: See the device test plan in 16-ANDROID-AUDIT.md.
findings.root_cause: No device lab in the workflow.
findings.impact: Camera/lifecycle/printing defects may exist that no test can show.
findings.recommended_remediation: Run the 16-ANDROID-AUDIT device checklist on a low-end and a mid-range phone before real sellers; Firebase Test Lab smoke tests in CI.
findings.regression_test: Device checklist results stored in audit/seller-app/evidence/device/.

findings.title: Approval gate fails open on profile load errors
findings.screen_workflow: App start for an unapproved seller while offline/slow or on any profile error
findings.description: The approval gate only shows 'Account Under Review' when a profile was loaded and is_approved=false. If getProfile throws (network, RLS, parse), the error is swallowed and the full operational dashboard renders.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T07 (profile error → dashboard with 'Add Product' and 'Verify Payments'), T06 control
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_home_shell_test.dart (T07).
findings.root_cause: Fail-open default (_profile == null treated as approved).
findings.impact: Server still blocks go-live (12.6 PASS) but unapproved sellers can prepare drops and upload images (see SA-SEC-003); approved sellers see an empty, error-less dashboard when offline.
findings.recommended_remediation: Three states: loading, error (retry), loaded; gate on loaded profile only.
findings.regression_test: T07 inverted.

findings.title: Weak password policy / no e-mail confirmation (local; hosted unknown)
findings.screen_workflow: Seller registration and login
findings.description: The repository's auth configuration allows 6-character passwords with no complexity and no e-mail confirmation. Hosted settings were not inspected and may differ.
findings.reproduction: Register with '123456'.
findings.root_cause: Local defaults; hosted unknown.
findings.impact: Seller accounts guard payments and buyer PII; weak passwords + public sign-up invite takeover.
findings.recommended_remediation: Hosted: min length ≥ 10 with leaked-password protection, e-mail confirmation on, rate limits; mirror in config.toml.
findings.regression_test: Hosted check script (auth settings via Management API).

findings.title: Payee UPI change without re-auth, notice or audit
findings.screen_workflow: Payment settings → change UPI VPA
findings.description: The payee VPA (where every buyer sends money) can be changed with just an active session: no re-authentication, no confirmation of the new VPA, no notification and no change history.
findings.reproduction: Change the VPA in Payment settings.
findings.root_cause: Sensitive setting treated like any profile field.
findings.impact: Account takeover (SA-SEC-002) or a borrowed phone redirects all buyer payments silently.
findings.recommended_remediation: Re-enter password (reauthenticate) for VPA/phone changes, e-mail notification, audit log table, warn while a drop is live.
findings.regression_test: Widget test requiring re-auth; SQL test of audit trigger.

findings.title: Floating Flutter, no migration job, no secret scan
findings.screen_workflow: Build and release
findings.description: Flutter channel 'stable' floats (no pinned version); no job applies/validates migrations; no secret scanning; the only artifact is a debug APK containing the staging URL and anon key, downloadable from a public repository.
findings.reproduction: Inspect workflow files.
findings.root_cause: Minimal CI.
findings.impact: Non-reproducible builds; schema drift; leaks (SA-SEC-002) not caught.
findings.recommended_remediation: Pin Flutter version; migration job against ephemeral Postgres; gitleaks; signed release artifact (SA-AND-001).
findings.regression_test: CI itself.

findings.title: No shared state; tabs never refresh after actions
findings.component: seller-app/lib/main.dart:321-351 (IndexedStack of 5 tabs); every screen loads in initState only
findings.screen_workflow: Switch tabs after an action
findings.description: There is no shared state or cache: each tab loads once in initState inside an IndexedStack and is never refreshed on focus. After verifying a payment, the Orders, Home and Products tabs keep showing old counts/states until pulled to refresh.
findings.reproduction: Verify a claim in Payments → switch to Orders: the order is still 'Pending'.
findings.root_cause: StatefulWidget-per-screen data loading without a store.
findings.impact: Seller acts on stale data (double handling, wrong announcements).
findings.recommended_remediation: A small app-level store (ChangeNotifier/Riverpod) fed by Realtime (SA-RT-001) with invalidation after mutations.
findings.regression_test: Widget test: mutation in one tab updates the others.

findings.title: Hosted schema state unverifiable
findings.screen_workflow: Deployed schema
findings.description: There is no deployment record or CI step proving that the hosted project matches migrations 001-033 (migrations are applied manually). This audit had no hosted database access, so hosted RLS/grants/functions are unverified.
findings.reproduction: Run 90_hosted_readonly_checks.sql in the SQL editor (read-only).
findings.root_cause: Manual deployment.
findings.impact: Every PROVEN-LOCAL result may differ in production.
findings.recommended_remediation: supabase db push from CI with a migration ledger check; run H1-H11 now.
findings.regression_test: CI drift check (supabase db diff).

findings.title: Closed drops can be reopened (docs forbid); wrong dialog copy
findings.screen_workflow: Drops → closed drop → 'Re-open Draft'
findings.description: Closed drops can be reopened (closed → draft → live) although docs/09 marks it 'Strictly Forbidden'. The confirmation dialog for re-opening reuses the closing text ('Closing this drop will stop new buyer reservations…').
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/12_lifecycle_guards.out: INFO 12.5 'close_drop=true then closed->draft=OK rows=1 then draft->live=OK rows=1'
findings.reproduction: Close a drop, tap Re-open Draft, then Go Live.
findings.root_cause: Safe-closure trigger only guards the transition into 'closed'.
findings.impact: Documentation/implementation conflict; analytics and buyer links of old drops reactivate; misleading dialog.
findings.recommended_remediation: Decide the rule (ADR): either forbid reopen in the trigger or document it; fix dialog copy per action.
findings.regression_test: Suite 12.5 expectation follows the decided rule.

findings.title: Drop slug editable while live
findings.screen_workflow: Edit a LIVE drop
findings.description: The public slug stays editable while the drop is live; the database accepts the change. Links already shared in the stream description, Instagram bio and WhatsApp broadcasts then 404.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/12_lifecycle_guards.out: INFO 12.4c 'slug change on LIVE drop -> OK rows=1'
findings.reproduction: Edit a live drop's slug and open the old link.
findings.root_cause: No status-aware lock on slug.
findings.impact: Buyers mid-live land on a 404.
findings.recommended_remediation: Lock slug once live (trigger + read-only field), or keep old slugs as redirects.
findings.regression_test: Suite 12.4c must fail for live drops.

findings.title: No pre-live readiness gate
findings.screen_workflow: Go Live
findings.description: Going live is not gated on readiness: unsynced/failed intake items (ADR-006 requires blocking), UPI disabled or not configured, zero products, or a missing stream URL are not checked or summarised.
evidence: docs/adr/ADR-006 'Drops cannot be transitioned to Live until all queued items reach synced status'
findings.reproduction: Queue an item offline and tap Go Live.
findings.root_cause: No pre-flight check.
findings.impact: Live starts with missing pieces or no payment route.
findings.recommended_remediation: Pre-flight sheet: N pieces live, M syncing/failed, UPI ON with VPA, link ready (copy/share) — block or warn.
findings.regression_test: Widget test for the pre-flight sheet.

findings.title: Seller verification and reaper deadlock
findings.component: Lock order: verify_manual_upi_payment (attempt → order) vs release_expired_holds (order → products → attempts)
findings.screen_workflow: Seller verifies a claim while the reaper runs
findings.description: The two functions lock rows in opposite order and deadlock; Postgres aborts one side. Because the reaper processes every expired order in one transaction, one deadlock rolls back the whole batch until the next run (hours today, SA-OPS-001).
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/14_concurrency.out: FINDING 14.3 'reaper session deadlock errors: 1 ; seller verify deadlock errors: 0'
findings.reproduction: 14_concurrency.sh scenario 14.3.
findings.root_cause: Inconsistent lock ordering; reaper not batched per order.
findings.impact: Missed hold releases or a failed seller verification (retry needed); more frequent once the reaper runs every minute.
findings.recommended_remediation: Adopt one lock order (order → products → attempts) everywhere; reaper commits per order (or uses SKIP LOCKED on attempts too) and retries on 40P01.
findings.regression_test: 14.3 must show zero deadlocks over N iterations.

findings.title: Mark Sold offered on reserved pieces; no undo
findings.screen_workflow: Products → piece → Mark Sold (sold on another channel)
findings.description: 'Mark Sold' is enabled for reserved pieces (the server answers PRODUCT_RESERVED, shown as a raw 'Error: …' snackbar) and there is no way to undo an accidental Mark Sold: no RPC returns a sold-offline piece to available.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/12_lifecycle_guards.out: INFO 12.9 'mark_product_sold_offline on a reserved piece -> PRODUCT_RESERVED'
findings.reproduction: Open a reserved piece → Mark Sold → Confirm.
findings.root_cause: Button state ignores 'reserved'; one-way RPC.
findings.impact: Confusing errors mid-live; a mis-tap permanently removes a garment from sale (principle 12: destructive actions need recovery).
findings.recommended_remediation: Disable Mark Sold for reserved pieces with an explanation; add an 'Undo sold offline' RPC within a time window (only if no order references the piece).
findings.regression_test: SQL test for undo RPC; widget test for disabled state.

findings.title: Add Product can silently target a closed drop
findings.screen_workflow: Home → Add Product (no live or draft drop)
findings.description: The target drop is chosen silently as live → draft → most recent of any status. If the latest drop is closed, new garments are attached to the closed drop and never appear to buyers; intake shows the drop title only in small grey text and offers no picker.
findings.reproduction: Close the only drop → Home → Add Product → save a piece → it belongs to the closed drop.
findings.root_cause: Convenience fallback without a status check.
findings.impact: Wasted intake work right before a live; seller confusion.
findings.recommended_remediation: Never target a closed drop: prompt to create a new drop or pick a draft; show the target drop prominently in intake with a switcher.
findings.regression_test: Widget test: with only a closed drop, Add Product opens Create Drop.

findings.title: Intake queue not idempotent; races and permanent errors loop forever
findings.screen_workflow: Intake sync after a timeout / with an invalid or duplicate code
findings.description: The queue does not distinguish permanent from transient errors and is not idempotent: if createProduct commits but the response is lost, the retry fails with DUPLICATE_PRODUCT_CODE forever although the product exists. The same end state is reached without any network fault when the seller reopens intake while a sync is still running: CameraIntakeScreen calls initialize() on the shared queue, which reloads items from disk and orphans the running sync's progress (T25); CHECK violations also loop with ≤64 s backoff indefinitely. The queue API has no way to edit or discard an item, so a permanently failing item can only be removed by clearing app data.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T25 'statusAfterFirstRun=uploading final=failed lastError=…DUPLICATE_PRODUCT_CODE serverProducts=1 createCalls=2' — CameraIntakeScreen re-initialises the shared queue (camera_intake_screen.dart:76) while a sync runs
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_offline_queue_test.dart (T16, T17).
findings.root_cause: No client-generated product id / idempotency key; no error classification.
findings.impact: Phantom failures, endless retries, battery/data use, seller distrust of the sync badge.
findings.recommended_remediation: Generate the product UUID client-side (insert with id) or send an idempotency key; on 23505 fetch the existing row and mark completed if it matches; classify 23514/22xxx as needs_edit.
findings.regression_test: T16 inverted: lost response → completed.

findings.title: Onboarding fee UTR only in auth metadata; SQL-only approval
findings.screen_workflow: Registration with ₹50 onboarding fee + UTR
findings.description: The onboarding-fee UTR is stored only in auth.users.raw_user_meta_data (the trigger does not copy it); there is no admin queue, no fee status on the profile and approval requires running admin_approve_seller in SQL.
findings.reproduction: Register; look for the UTR in public tables.
findings.root_cause: Manual, out-of-band process.
findings.impact: Fee checks are error-prone; paid sellers wait, unpaid ones may be approved.
findings.recommended_remediation: seller_applications table (fee UTR, amount, status, reviewer, timestamps) + operator view/script; tell the seller the status.
findings.regression_test: SQL test: sign-up creates an application row.

findings.title: Suspension does not stop a live drop selling
findings.screen_workflow: Operator suspends a seller who has a live drop
findings.description: Setting is_approved=false hides the catalogue rows, but the drop stays live and checkout does not check approval, so orders keep being created.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/12_lifecycle_guards.out: FINDING 12.7 'after admin_approve_seller(B,false)=true: catalog rows visible=0 but checkout success=true (drop still live=live)'
findings.reproduction: Suite 12.7.
findings.root_cause: Approval checked only on go-live and in public views.
findings.impact: Suspension (fraud response) is ineffective.
findings.recommended_remediation: Checkout and payment RPCs must require is_seller_approved; suspension should close live drops via the safe-closure path.
findings.regression_test: Suite 12.7 expects SELLER_SUSPENDED.

findings.title: No operator tooling; approvals and refunds need SQL
findings.screen_workflow: Approve/suspend sellers, review onboarding fee, resolve stuck orders, refunds, late claims
findings.description: There is no admin UI. Approvals, suspensions, onboarding-fee checks (UTR stored only in auth metadata), stuck reservations, refunds and data fixes all require the Supabase SQL editor.
evidence: grep admin_ in migrations → admin_approve_seller only
findings.reproduction: Try to approve a seller or find a seller's onboarding UTR without SQL.
findings.root_cause: Out of MVP scope; no runbooks.
findings.impact: Slow, error-prone operations; risky manual SQL against production during incidents.
findings.recommended_remediation: Minimal operator console (or a few service-role scripts) for: pending sellers with UTR, approve/suspend, stuck holds, refund-owed list, late claims; written runbooks.
findings.regression_test: Runbook drills on staging.

findings.title: No tested backup/restore; free-tier pause risk
findings.screen_workflow: Database loss, project pause, accidental destructive SQL
findings.description: No documented backup/restore procedure or restore drill exists; the project relies on a keep-alive cron to avoid free-tier pausing, and free-tier projects have no point-in-time recovery.
findings.reproduction: n/a (absence).
findings.root_cause: Zero-cost constraint without compensating procedures.
findings.impact: A paused or damaged project during a live stops all selling; data loss risk for orders/payments.
findings.recommended_remediation: Scheduled logical dumps (pg_dump via GitHub Action to encrypted storage), documented and rehearsed restore, consider Pro tier before real volume.
findings.regression_test: Quarterly restore drill into a scratch project.

findings.title: Times shown in UTC (cards, labels, analytics)
findings.screen_workflow: Order cards, shipping labels, analytics day buckets
findings.description: Timestamps from PostgREST are UTC and are formatted without toLocal(): order times read 5 h 30 min early, labels carry UTC times, and analytics 'Today'/daily bars start at 05:30 IST.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T04 'createdAt.isUtc=true card text=09:00 AM local=02:30 PM', T05
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_timezone_test.dart with TZ=Asia/Kolkata.
findings.root_cause: DateFormat on UTC DateTime.
findings.impact: Wrong times when matching buyer messages/UPI timestamps; wrong daily sales.
findings.recommended_remediation: Convert to local (or explicit Asia/Kolkata) at the model boundary; compute day buckets in IST.
findings.regression_test: T04/T05 inverted.

findings.title: WhatsApp drops +91 for numbers starting with 91
findings.screen_workflow: Contact buyer on WhatsApp
findings.description: The app assumes a number starting with '91' already has the country code. Checkout stores 10-digit numbers (022 strips +91), so every valid mobile beginning with 91 (e.g. 91234 56789) is sent to WhatsApp without +91 and reaches a wrong or invalid number.
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_order_details_test.dart (T02).
findings.root_cause: Heuristic prefix check instead of length-based normalisation.
findings.impact: Payment reminders and dispatch messages go to strangers (privacy) or fail.
findings.recommended_remediation: If 10 digits → prefix 91; if 12 digits starting 91 → keep; share one helper.
findings.regression_test: T02 inverted plus table-driven unit test.

findings.title: Order details crash on names with double spaces
findings.screen_workflow: Open an order whose buyer name contains two consecutive spaces
findings.description: split(' ') yields an empty part and parts[1][0] throws RangeError during build: the order screen fails to render (red screen in debug, grey box in release).
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T01 'RangeError (index): Invalid value: Valid value range is empty: 0'
findings.reproduction: Buyer name 'Priya  Sharma' (accepted by checkout, which only trims ends).
findings.root_cause: Unsafe string indexing.
findings.impact: Seller cannot open that order to verify, contact or ship.
findings.recommended_remediation: split(RegExp(r'\s+')) with empty-part filtering; fuzz test names.
findings.regression_test: T01 inverted.

findings.title: Cancelled/expired/refund-owed orders hidden
findings.screen_workflow: Orders tab
findings.description: Only Pending/Paid/Ready/Shipped tabs exist; cancelled and expired orders (released holds, rejected claims, forfeited advances, refund-owed late payments) are not shown anywhere.
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_kanban_test.dart (T20).
findings.root_cause: Tab filters only cover the happy path.
findings.impact: No history for disputes, no visibility of forfeited advances or refunds owed.
findings.recommended_remediation: 'Closed' tab or filter with reasons (expired, released, rejected, refund owed).
findings.regression_test: T20 inverted.

findings.title: UI order actions don't match the server state machine
findings.screen_workflow: Paid tab → Dispatch / 4×6 Label; Order details → 'Mark as Ready'
findings.description: Client affordances do not match the server state machine: Dispatch and label printing are offered for advance-paid orders with balance due (server answers ORDER_NOT_PAID after the seller fills the form); 'Mark as Ready' opens the dispatch dialog and is shown for every non-shipped status including pending; there is no separate pack/ready step — dispatch chains mark_order_ready_to_ship and mark_order_shipped as two non-atomic calls.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T03 ('Mark as Ready' → 'Dispatch & Print Label'), T21 (Dispatch shown for advance-paid)
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_order_details_test.dart (T03), audit_kanban_test.dart (T21).
findings.root_cause: UI derives actions from status alone, not from payment/fulfilment state.
findings.impact: Wasted taps and confusing errors; the label for an advance-paid order says PREPAID (SA-SHIP-002).
findings.recommended_remediation: Derive actions from (status, payment_status, fulfilment_status) exactly as the RPCs do; 'Collect balance' for advance-paid; real 'Mark packed' step.
findings.regression_test: Table-driven widget test of actions per state.

findings.title: Verification card lacks type, garment, deadline and consequences
findings.screen_workflow: Payments tab → claim card → Verify / Reject
findings.description: The card does not give the seller what is needed to decide: every claim is labelled 'Advance Payment' even for full/balance payments; a generic hanger icon instead of the garment; 'Screenshot: Tap to view' opens a hard-coded placeholder, not a buyer screenshot; no time remaining; no order status (late claims do not say the order is cancelled or whether the garment is still available); 'Paid on' is the claim time. The confirm dialog shows only amount and order code.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T09 (full claim labelled 'Advance Payment'), T12 (placeholder screenshot), T13 (no garment code/image)
findings.reproduction: Run audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_payment_queue_test.dart.
findings.root_cause: UI built before payment types/late claims; repository query does not join order items/products.
findings.impact: Wrong decisions under time pressure (verifying the wrong amount type, verifying a late claim that triggers a refund, not knowing which buyer/garment).
findings.recommended_remediation: Show payment type, amount expected vs order total, garment thumbnail + code, buyer phone, time remaining, late/refund consequence; remove the fake screenshot or implement real upload; put Verify/Reject at thumb reach.
findings.regression_test: Widget tests: label follows payment_type; card renders code/thumbnail; late claim shows consequence text.

findings.title: Reject always releases the hold (no 'ask to fix' path)
findings.screen_workflow: Payments → Reject
findings.description: Every rejection releases the hold and cancels the order. The RPC supports p_release_hold=false, but the UI never offers 'keep the reservation and ask the buyer to resubmit'. A buyer who mistyped one digit of the UTR loses the garment instantly.
findings.reproduction: Reject any claim from the Payments tab.
findings.root_cause: UI does not expose the existing RPC option.
findings.impact: Lost sales and buyer frustration from typos; no recovery path.
findings.recommended_remediation: Two explicit actions: 'Ask buyer to fix UTR (keep hold N min)' and 'Reject & release'; show the consequence in the dialog.
findings.regression_test: Widget test: choosing 'keep hold' calls reject with releaseHold:false.

findings.title: Duplicate-UTR check is case-sensitive and verify-time only
findings.screen_workflow: Buyer submits UTR; seller verifies
findings.description: The same UTR can be submitted on any number of orders (no claim-time check), and the verify-time reuse check is an exact, case-sensitive string match: a lower-case variant of an already verified reference is accepted on a different order.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/13_payments.out: INFO 13.3a (second order accepted the same UTR at claim time), PASS 13.3b (exact duplicate blocked at verify), FINDING 13.3c (lower-case variant verified on another order)
findings.reproduction: Suite 13.3.
findings.root_cause: No normalisation (upper/trim) and no unique index on normalised verified references; no claim-time duplicate warning.
findings.impact: One bank transfer can be presented for two orders; the seller must catch it manually.
findings.recommended_remediation: Normalise UTRs (upper, strip spaces) at claim and verify; unique index on normalised verified reference; flag 'UTR already used on order X' in the seller card.
findings.regression_test: Suite 13.3c must return REFERENCE_USED_ON_ANOTHER_ORDER.

findings.title: UPI disabled still accepts reservations
findings.component: create_order_with_reservation (022) vs initiate_payment_attempt (013) + Payment settings toggle (seller-app/lib/presentation/payment_settings_screen.dart:205-230)
findings.screen_workflow: Seller toggles 'UPI enabled' off (or an attacker does via SA-SEC-001) during a live
findings.description: When upi_enabled=false, checkout still reserves pieces but no payment attempt can be created (UPI_DISABLED). Buyers hold pieces they cannot pay for until the reaper runs (hours, SA-OPS-001).
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/13_payments.out: INFO 13.13 'upi_enabled=false: checkout success=true (piece reserved) but initiate_payment_attempt -> UPI_DISABLED'
findings.reproduction: Suite 13.13.
findings.root_cause: Payment availability not checked at reservation time; no warning in settings while a drop is live.
findings.impact: Whole-catalogue lock-up and lost sales; amplifies SA-SEC-001.
findings.recommended_remediation: Reject checkout when UPI is disabled (or a payment method is not configured); warn in Payment settings when a drop is live.
findings.regression_test: Suite 13.13 must return a checkout error.

findings.title: WhatsApp reminder: wrong amount, raw UPI ID, no order link
findings.screen_workflow: Orders → Pending → WhatsApp
findings.description: The reminder quotes the order total even when only an advance is due, embeds the seller's raw UPI ID (hidden from the public API since migration 033) and contains no link to the buyer's order/payment page. Buyers who pay the UPI ID directly create a payment the system cannot match to an attempt; the order still expires.
evidence: order_card.dart:85 totalPaisa; 87,92 profile.upiId; 97 wa.me link without order URL
findings.reproduction: Tap WhatsApp on a pending advance order and read the message.
findings.root_cause: Reminder written before the payment-attempt/claim flow.
findings.impact: Over-payment requests, unmatched payments, manual reconciliation, expired orders that were actually paid.
findings.recommended_remediation: Send the buyer's order link (token URL) and the amount actually due; let the buyer pay and claim on the order page.
findings.regression_test: Widget test of the generated message for advance and full orders.

findings.title: Refund-owed ledger rows deletable through order deletion
findings.component: orders_seller_delete policy (supabase/migrations/008_enable_rls_and_policies.sql:154-164) + prevent_finalized_order_deletion (supabase/migrations/010_seller_storefront_and_order_state_machine.sql:274-281) + order_payments FK ON DELETE CASCADE (010:210)
findings.screen_workflow: Direct API call with the seller's own session (no UI path today)
findings.description: Sellers may DELETE their own orders unless the status is confirmed/paid/shipped/expired. Since migration 023 a verified late claim can leave an order 'cancelled' with payment_status 'paid' and a verified ledger row (refund owed). Deleting that order cascades and erases the verified ledger row — the only record that the buyer's money was received.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/17_ledger_deletion.out: FINDING 17.1 'seller DELETE of a refund-owed order (refund_required=true) -> OK rows=1 | verified ledger rows before=1 after=0'; PASS 17.2 (expired advance order protected), PASS 17.3 (paid order protected)
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/sql/17_ledger_deletion.sql (17.1).
findings.root_cause: Deletion guard keyed on order status only; ledger cascades with its order; the 023 refund state was not considered.
findings.impact: Evidence of received money can be erased (dishonest seller avoiding a refund, or a future 'clean up cancelled orders' feature); breaks the 'ledger is immutable' invariant.
findings.recommended_remediation: Block deletion of any order that has order_payments rows (or payment_status <> 'unpaid'); change order_payments FK to ON DELETE RESTRICT; consider removing the seller DELETE policy entirely (soft-cancel only).
findings.regression_test: Suite 17.1 must fail with a guard error and keep the ledger row.

findings.title: Unpaginated nested order downloads (~2.4 MB per season)
findings.component: seller-app/lib/data/repositories/seller_repository.dart:760-820 (getAllOrders), callers: dashboard (x2 via getRecentActivity), Kanban, analytics, Shipping shortcut, every realtime event
findings.screen_workflow: Home, Orders, Analytics after a few months of selling
findings.description: getAllOrders has no limit or pagination and embeds order_items + products. One season (20 drops × 100 pieces, 2,000 orders) returns ≈2.4 MB of JSON per call; analytics is computed in Dart from the full history on the UI isolate.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/15_perf_seller_queries.out: 'INFO 15.1 getAllOrders(): 2000 orders, ~2473 KB JSON, 144 ms' (server side, dev host; 143 ms in an earlier run)
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/sql/15_perf_seller_queries.sql.
findings.root_cause: Convenience queries; no server-side aggregation.
findings.impact: Multi-second loads and jank on 4G/low-end phones exactly when the seller is busiest; mobile data use.
findings.recommended_remediation: Drop-scoped and status-scoped pagination; counts via RPC (seller_dashboard_summary); analytics via SQL aggregates; JSON parsing off the UI isolate.
findings.regression_test: Suite 15 budget assertions; widget test that dashboard issues ≤ N requests.
findings.confidence: Medium (server timing measured; device parsing time inferred).

findings.title: No reconnect/catch-up; full refetch per realtime event
findings.screen_workflow: Kanban with a drop selected
findings.description: The subscription has no status/reconnect handling (onStatusChanged is never passed), no catch-up fetch after backgrounding or network loss, parse errors are swallowed, and every INSERT/UPDATE event triggers a full unpaginated refetch of the drop's orders with nested items.
findings.reproduction: Select a drop, toggle airplane mode for 60 s while an order is placed, return: the Kanban stays stale until manual refresh (INFERRED; device test required).
findings.root_cause: Minimal channel wrapper.
findings.impact: Silent staleness after network blips; event storms during busy lives (each event = full list download).
findings.recommended_remediation: Track channel status, show a 'Live updates paused' banner, refetch on SUBSCRIBED after reconnect/resume; apply event payloads incrementally; debounce refetches.
findings.regression_test: Unit test of the session store with simulated CLOSED/SUBSCRIBED transitions.

findings.title: Unapproved accounts can upload to the public product-images bucket
findings.component: Storage policies product_images_seller_insert/update (supabase/migrations/027_product_multi_images_and_storage.sql:28-40; 018:36-52) + open sign-up (supabase/config.toml:175 enable_signup=true)
findings.screen_workflow: Registration → any authenticated account → Storage upload
findings.description: The insert/update policies on the public product-images bucket only check that the first folder equals auth.uid(). Any self-registered, unapproved account can therefore upload JPEG/PNG/WebP files up to 5 MB that are publicly readable from the project's storage domain.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/11_seller_isolation.out: FINDING 11.5b unapproved seller C uploaded to product-images; PASS 11.5a cross-folder write rejected
findings.reproduction: Register a seller (unapproved), upload to product-images/<uid>/x.jpg with the anon key + session, open the public URL.
findings.root_cause: Storage policies do not call public.is_seller_approved(auth.uid()).
findings.impact: Free public hosting for arbitrary images under the LiveDrop Supabase domain (phishing/abuse content), storage and egress quota consumption on the free tier.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add AND public.is_seller_approved(auth.uid()) to insert/update policies; add per-seller object quota or size budget; consider CAPTCHA/invite-only sign-up while onboarding is manual.
findings.regression_test: Suite 11.5b must report rejection for an unapproved seller.
findings.confidence: High (local DB with Supabase storage schema stand-in).

findings.title: EXIF (device, GPS) published with product photos
findings.screen_workflow: Camera / gallery intake → public product image
findings.description: The intake pipeline re-encodes images with the pure-Dart image package, which carries the decoded EXIF block (device make/model, GPS) into the output that is published in the public bucket.
findings.reproduction: Import a gallery photo that has GPS EXIF → save product → download the public URL → exiftool shows GPS and camera model.
findings.root_cause: No EXIF stripping before encoding.
findings.impact: Many boutiques operate from home; publishing GPS coordinates of the seller's home/shop to every catalog viewer is a personal-safety risk.
findings.recommended_remediation: Clear EXIF before encoding (orientation is already baked during decode, see T22); add a unit test asserting no GPS/Make tags in output.
findings.regression_test: Invert T23: output must contain no GPS IFD and no Make/Model tags.
findings.confidence: High for the pipeline; Medium for frequency (camera-plugin captures may lack GPS; gallery images commonly carry it).

findings.title: Anyone can list every stored image, including unpublished drops
findings.component: Storage policy product_images_public_read (supabase/migrations/027_product_multi_images_and_storage.sql:23-26: FOR SELECT TO public USING bucket_id='product-images')
findings.screen_workflow: Anyone (anon key) listing the product-images bucket
findings.description: The SELECT policy on storage.objects covers every object in the bucket for every role. The Storage list/search API is evaluated under RLS, so an anonymous visitor can enumerate all folders and files: seller UUIDs, drop UUIDs, photos of draft (unpublished) drops and anything unapproved accounts uploaded. Public URLs of a public bucket do not need this policy.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/18_storage_enumeration.out: FINDING 18.1 'anon can list 2 object(s) … incl. draft-drop and unapproved-seller paths'; PASS 18.2 (the draft drop itself is hidden from anon)
findings.reproduction: Local: tests/sql/18_storage_enumeration.sql. Hosted (read-only): POST $SUPABASE_URL/storage/v1/object/list/product-images with the anon key and {"prefix":""} — a secure project returns [] (or 400/403).
findings.root_cause: Read policy written for public downloads, which public buckets already allow without RLS.
findings.impact: Pre-launch inventory and prices-to-be leak before the live (competitors, spoilers); combined with SA-SEC-004, GPS-tagged originals of unpublished pieces are enumerable; free CDN for abusive uploads (SA-SEC-003).
findings.recommended_remediation: Drop the anon/public SELECT policy (public object URLs keep working); if listing is needed, restrict it to the owning seller ((storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text).
findings.regression_test: Suite 18.1 must list 0 objects for anon; hosted list call returns [].
findings.confidence: High (local, Storage API behaviour per Supabase docs; hosted list call not executed).

findings.title: Label prints PREPAID on balance-due orders; fake barcode
findings.screen_workflow: Print 4×6 label
findings.description: Every label states 'PREPAID - DO NOT COLLECT CASH' and the order total, even for advance-paid orders with a balance due; when no AWB is entered the barcode encodes 'TRK-<order code>', which no courier can scan; the date is UTC.
findings.reproduction: Print a label for a confirmed (advance-paid) order without tracking.
findings.root_cause: Label assumes the fully-prepaid happy path.
findings.impact: Courier will not collect the balance; unusable barcodes; label disputes.
findings.recommended_remediation: Only print PREPAID when balance_due=0 (block otherwise); require a real AWB before printing a barcode; local time.
findings.regression_test: Golden/unit test on label content per payment state.

findings.title: Tests don't cover money, inventory, auth or concurrency
findings.component: seller-app/test (49 tests), buyer-web tests (655), no DB test suite
findings.screen_workflow: Regression safety
findings.description: Existing tests pass but do not cover the risky paths: late claims, claim expiry, reaper/verify races, view privileges, threshold parity, timezone, permanent queue failures, approval fail-open, action/state matrix. Migrations are not applied or tested in CI.
findings.reproduction: Compare the matrix in 20-TEST-COVERAGE-AUDIT.md.

findings.screen_workflow: Running a live

findings.title: Analytics not ledger-based; UTC days
findings.screen_workflow: More → Analytics

findings.title: Docs claim features the code lacks

findings.description: Documentation claims are contradicted by code: RTM marks realtime dashboard/kanban, password reset, offline queue and mark_order_paid as Implemented; docs/14 specifies a seller-scoped channel 'seller:{seller_id}:orders' (code: per-drop 'seller-orders-<dropId>'); docs/09 forbids reopening closed drops (allowed); ADR-005/006 differ from implementation; seven referenced reports (e.g. TASK-2.5A-STAGING-VALIDATION-REPORT.md, FINAL-RELEASE-CANDIDATE-REPORT.md) do not exist.

findings.title: live->draft bypasses safe closure (API)
findings.screen_workflow: API (no UI button today)
findings.description: A live drop can be set back to draft by direct UPDATE without the safe-closure protocol, leaving reservations and claims attached to a drop buyers can no longer open.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/12_lifecycle_guards.out: INFO 12.4b 'live -> draft direct UPDATE (unpublish without releasing holds) -> OK rows=1'
findings.reproduction: Suite 12.4b.
findings.root_cause: Only the transition to 'closed' is guarded.
findings.impact: Stranded holds/claims if a future UI or script uses it.
findings.recommended_remediation: Route all status changes through RPCs (go_live, close_drop, unpublish with the same claim-preserving rules).
findings.regression_test: Suite 12.4b must fail.

findings.title: Products insertable directly as sold/reserved
findings.component: products INSERT RLS policy (supabase/migrations/008_enable_rls_and_policies.sql) + enforce_products_inventory_immutability (025, UPDATE only)
findings.screen_workflow: Direct API insert by an authenticated seller
findings.description: A seller can insert products already 'sold' or 'reserved' (with no order). Reserved pieces without an order are never released by the reaper, which works from orders.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/12_lifecycle_guards.out: FINDING 12.3 'seller can INSERT product already sold (OK rows=1) / reserved with no order (OK rows=1)'
findings.reproduction: Suite 12.3.

findings.screen_workflow: Long-term use; Settings → Clear Image Cache
findings.description: Completed queue items and their local JPEGs are never pruned, so storage grows with every garment (0.5-1.2 MB per angle in T24, up to 4 angles); 'Clear Image Cache' only shows a success snackbar.

findings.title: No balance-collection tool for advance orders
findings.screen_workflow: Advance-paid order with balance due
findings.description: The seller has no tool to request the balance: no 'send balance link', no balance amount in the reminder, and the WhatsApp reminder is only on pending orders. Balance payment depends on the buyer returning to the order page on their own.

findings.reproduction: Open a confirmed advance-paid order.
findings.root_cause: Feature gap.

findings.title: Image output above ADR-005 / docs-22 budgets
findings.screen_workflow: Rapid intake (up to 4 angles per garment)
findings.description: ADR-005 specifies WebP q80 at < 150-200 KB; the implementation emits JPEG q85. On textured synthetic photos the dev host produced 552 KB (1280×720 input) and 1.16 MB (12 MP input) in 0.39-3.0 s; docs/22 budgets < 600 ms and < 250 KB on a Redmi 9A-class phone. Sizes for real fabric photos will be lower than this noisy worst case but still above budget at q85/1200 px.
evidence: audit/seller-app/evidence/flutter-audit-tests.out: SA-AUD-T24 '1280x720 … -> 720x720 552KB in 389 ms', '4000x3000 … -> 1200x1200 1158KB in 3000 ms (dev host)'
findings.reproduction: audit/seller-app/tests/flutter/audit_image_perf_test.dart.
findings.root_cause: Pure-Dart encoder and settings differ from the ADR.
findings.impact: Slower uploads on 4G, higher storage/egress on the free tier, slower buyer catalogue.
findings.recommended_remediation: Native compression (flutter_image_compress) to WebP/JPEG q75-80, 1080-1200 px; measure on target devices.
findings.regression_test: Size/time budget test on fixture photos + device benchmark.

findings.title: Silent fee fallbacks; profile threshold not editable

findings.title: Small touch targets; actions out of thumb reach
findings.component: Order card (40 dp buttons), payment card (44 dp), app-bar refresh icons, Kanban search/dropdown at top
findings.screen_workflow: One-handed use while holding a garment

findings.title: Camera lifecycle needs device validation
findings.screen_workflow: Camera intake while notifications/calls/app switcher interrupt
findings.description: On AppLifecycleState.inactive the controller is disposed but the field is not cleared and _isCameraInitialized stays true; resume re-initialises asynchronously without awaiting or error handling, and _initCamera calls setState without a mounted check on the empty-camera path. Pattern follows the plugin example but needs device validation for 'used after dispose' errors and black previews on low-end phones.

findings.title: Back exits the app; lost picker data; no orientation lock
findings.component: seller-app/lib/main.dart:319-375 (tab shell without PopScope); camera_intake_screen.dart:236-243 (image_picker fallback without retrieveLostData); no orientation lock
findings.screen_workflow: System Back during a live; process death while the system camera is open; rotation
findings.description: System Back on any tab exits the app (no return-to-Home step, no confirmation while a drop is live). When the camera plugin is unavailable the image_picker fallback launches the system camera; if Android kills LiveDrop meanwhile, the photo is lost because retrieveLostData() is not used. No orientation lock and no landscape layouts.
findings.reproduction: Device: open Orders tab, press Back; enable 'Don't keep activities' and capture via the fallback path.
findings.root_cause: Default Navigator/ImagePicker behaviour.
findings.impact: Accidental exits mid-live; occasional lost captures on low-memory phones.
findings.recommended_remediation: PopScope on the shell (Back → Home tab, confirm exit while live); call ImagePicker.retrieveLostData() on start; lock portrait.
findings.regression_test: Widget test for Back behaviour; device checklist.

findings.title: close_drop result ignored by the app

The drop page queries only status='live', so a draft or closed drop renders 'not found' (the 'closed' branch in page.tsx is unreachable) instead of 'starts soon' / 'this drop has ended'.
